svg.text: K5 Ram-and-die column — how the mechanisms work
Six looping close-ups (section views). Numbers are the paper estimates of the concept document; nothing is built yet.
1 Push through the die, cut off
One layer of potatoes lies on the grid. The ram pushes a
loose piston on top; sticks come out under the die and each
turn of the sickle cuts one row of dice into the pot below.
Slice thickness = ram advance per turn.
bore 140 × 300 · 8 kN ram · 1.5 kg diced ≈ 3 min
2 Turret and die carousel (top view)

g.text: the tube rides on its die
the tube rides on its die

svg.text: Three loose tubes stand in a turret, six loose dies in a
carousel below. Turning both carries a tube on its die;
turning the carousel alone changes the die. Its rear third
runs under a wash hood, so dies are washed in passing.
carousel Ø400 · 1 actuator each · force via die to deck
3 Kneading by back-extrusion
The tube stands on a blank cap. The ram strokes a plunger
that is smaller than the bore: the dough must flow up through
the gap and is stretched, then folds as the plunger lifts.
Untested for bread dough (L–M); mince mass M–H.
1–2.4 kN · 3.5 s/stroke · 1.6 kg dough 8–17 min
4 Patties: extrude and cut

g.text: pan held and indexed by the shuttle fork

svg.text: The mixed mince stays in its tube. Over the Ø80 former the
ram advances 7 mm, the wire bow cuts the strand, the puck
drops 60 mm onto the oiled pan, the shuttle moves the pan on.
Same principle: dumplings Ø45, Spätzle, piping, paste doses.
8 patties in 50 s · 12 in 75 s (PRP-023: 5 min)
5 Frying book: flip everything at once

g.text: 1 leaf R closes over leaf L
turned: crust up, second side fries

svg.text: Two GN 1/2 pans on hinged leaves over two induction coils.
Closing the book and opening the other side turns every
piece at once; nothing goes under the food. The same book
breads cutlets, flattens meat (1.5 kN) and presses dough.
GN 1/2 leaves · 60 Nm = 2 kN · 6 s per flip
6 Pigging and tube wash in place
The piston pushes to the bottom rim and wipes the bore (film
≈ 50 µm). At SERVICE a spray dasher pushes it out into the
parts basket and washes the bore; one camera image checks it.
Pots, pans and tools go to the central ware washer.
≈ 5.5 L and 5 min per tube · 85 °C rinse: A0 ≥ 60
